title: Water Use for Neonatal Feeding — Women and Infants 6 West

fields.organization: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center — Women and Infants 6 West
fields.location: Women and Infants 6 West, 6 West, Tower B
fields.summary: The Women and Infants 6 West unit has 18 bassinets occupied and 32 mothers in postpartum recovery. All infant feeding uses powdered formula prepared with tap water. We have 220 ready-to-feed bottles in stock and use approximately 600 per day. NICU feeding uses sterile water from Pharmacy. Breast pump cleaning and hand hygiene require tap water. The Do Not Drink advisory prevents safe use of tap water for formula preparation and cleaning. We request ready-to-feed formula and sterile water for the unit through Sunday to maintain infant feeding safety and prevent cross-contamination.

findings.notes: Powdered formula must be mixed with potable water. Tap water is under Do Not Drink advisory.
Pharmacy-supplied sterile water for NICU remains available.
Cleaning protocol requires tap water; current advisory prohibits use.
Tap water used in sinks for handwashing; water is unsafe per advisory.
No education materials distributed on safe feeding alternatives.
Oral care for infants not permitted with tap water.
No stock of disposable wipe sets for pump cleaning.
Non-compliant water use increases risk of gastrointestinal infection in newborns.
No alternative formula supply on site.
No contact made with Pharmacy for sterile water delivery.

actionsTaken: Notified Hospital Command Center (HCC) of feeding risk
Issued internal alert to nursing leadership
Paired with Nutrition Services for emergency formula request
recommendations: Immediate delivery of 1,000 ready-to-feed bottles to Women and Infants 6 West
Arrange for sterile water delivery to unit via Pharmacy
Activate regional supplier network through the healthcare coalition
Implement disposable cleaning kits for breast pump and equipment
Update infection prevention policy for neonatal unit under Do Not Drink advisory
fields.photosNote: 2 photos attached: IMG_WI6W-01 (bassinet row), IMG_WI6W-02 (formula preparation station)
fields.signature: Carla Dunn, Nurse Manager, Women and Infants 6 West

instructorNote: This inject reveals a critical care gap in neonatal feeding. The CNO and AOC must act on the supply request immediately, as infants are at high risk of dehydration and infection. Watch for delayed action on sterile water and formula procurement.
